The meaning of ﴿Then We made the drop a clinging clot﴾ is that He, glorified is He, transformed the white drop into a red clot. ﴿Then We made the clot a lump﴾, that is, a piece of flesh not yet shaped. ﴿Then We made the lump bones﴾, that is, Allah, glorified is He, made them hard so that they would be a backbone for the body, in specific shapes. ﴿Then We clothed the bones with flesh﴾, that is, Allah, glorified is He, caused flesh to grow over every bone in the amount that suits it and befits it. ﴿Then We brought him into being as another creation﴾, that is, We breathed into him the spirit after he had been an inanimate thing. It was said: We brought him out into the world. It was said: it is the growth of hair. It was said: it is the emergence of teeth. It was said: it is the completion of the powers created in him. There is no obstacle to intending all of these. The use of thumma (then) indicates the great difference between the two creations. ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾, that is, He deserves glorification and praise.

It was said: it is derived from barakah (blessing), that is, His good and blessing are abundant. Al-khalq in the language means measurement (taqdir). It is said: "I measured (khalaqtu) the hide" when you measure it in order to cut a piece from it. So the meaning of "the best of creators" is: the most skilful of makers who measure. From this is the words of the poet:
"Indeed you cut what you measure, and some people measure and then do not cut."

﴿Then indeed you, after that, will surely die.﴾ The reference in His words "after that" is to the preceding matters, that is: then indeed you, after those matters, are surely those who will go to death without doubt.

﴿Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, will be raised﴾ from your graves to the place of gathering (al-mahshar) for the reckoning and the punishment.

The lam in ﴿And We had certainly created above you seven paths﴾ is the answer to an omitted oath, and the sentence is independent, containing an explanation of the creation of what they need after the explanation of their own creation. The tara'iq (paths) are the heavens.

Al-Khalili, al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: they were called tara'iq because some of them were layered (tuwriqa) above others, like the layers of a shoe sole (mutarraqat al-na'l).

Abu 'Ubaydah said: "I layered (tarraqtu) the thing," meaning I made some of it above others, and the Arabs call everything above something else a tariqah.

It was said: because they are the paths of the angels. It was said: because they are the paths of the stars.

﴿And We were not unaware of the creation﴾. Here "creation" means the created things, that is: We were not unaware of these seven paths and their keeping from falling onto the earth.

Most of the exegetes said: what is meant is that We are not unaware of all creation; rather, We preserved the heavens from falling, and We preserved those on the earth from the sky falling on them and destroying them, or the earth shaking with them, or them perishing by some cause that would uproot them. It is permissible that what is intended is the negation of heedlessness regarding the maintenance of their interests and what they live by, and the negation of heedlessness regarding their protection.

﴿And We sent down from the sky water﴾. This is among the blessings with which Allah, glorified is He, favoured His creatures. What is meant by water is rainwater, for by it is the life of the earth and of the animals in it. Among that is the water of the rivers that descend from the sky, and of the springs and wells that are extracted from the earth, for their origin is from the water of the sky.

It was said: by this verse He, glorified is He, intended the four rivers: Sayhan, Jayhan, the Euphrates and the Nile. But there is no basis for this specification.

It was said: what is meant is sweet water. But there is no basis for that either, for there is no water on earth except that it is from the sky. The meaning of "in a measure" (bi-qadar) is by a measure from Us, or in an amount by which there is the welfare of crops and fruits, for if it were abundant it would bring about the destruction of that. Similar to it is His words, glorified is He: ﴿And there is nothing but that its treasuries are with Us, and We send it down only in a known measure﴾. The meaning of ﴿then We caused it to settle in the earth﴾ is We made it lodged in it, so that they benefit from it at the time of their need for it, like the water that remains in pools and puddles and the like. ﴿And indeed We are able to take it away﴾, that is, just as We were able to send it down, so We are able to take it away in some manner. The indefinite form here has a beautiful effect that is not hidden. In this is a severe threat, because of what it indicates of His power, glorified is He, to remove it and sink it deep, until people perish of thirst and their livestock perish. Similar to it is His words: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if your water should become sunken, who would bring you clear water?﴾

Then He, glorified is He, explained what results from the sending down of water, saying: ﴿So We produced for you therewith gardens of palm trees and grapevines﴾, that is, We brought into being with that water gardens of the two kinds mentioned, for you, ﴿in them there are abundant fruits﴾ with which you enjoy yourselves and of which you eat.

It was said: the meaning is: from these gardens are the sources of your sustenance and livelihood, like His words: "So-and-so eats from such-and-such a trade." This is far-fetched. He, glorified is He, limited the mention to palms and grapes because they are the ones found in al-Ta'if and al-Madinah and what is connected to them.

Thus said Ibn Jarir. It was also said: because they are the noblest of trees in fruit, and the best of them in benefit, taste and pleasure.

It was said that what is meant by His words ﴿for you in them are fruits﴾ is that for you in these gardens are fruits other than grapes and palms.

It was said: the meaning is that for you in these two kinds in particular are fruits, because in them are varieties differing in taste and colour.

The jurists have differed greatly over what the word "fruit" (fakihah) applies to. The best of what has been said is that it applies to the fruits that people eat, which are not a staple for them, nor food, nor condiment. Disagreement arose over whether vegetables (buqul) enter into fruit or not.

As for the accusative of shajarah (tree), it is in coordination with jannat (gardens). Al-Farra' permitted the nominative on the assumption: "and there is a tree," so it is raised as a subject (mubtada') whose predicate is omitted and estimated before it, which is the mentioned adverbial phrase.

Al-Wahidi said: all the exegetes say that what is meant by this tree is the olive tree. It was singled out for mention because no one tends it with irrigation, and it is the one from which oil is extracted. Allah, glorified is He, mentioned it as a favour upon His servants; and because it is the most noble of trees, the most widely beneficial, and the most abundant in blessing.

Then He, glorified is He, described this tree as ﴿coming forth from Mount Sinai﴾, which is a mountain in Bayt al-Maqdis. In the speech of the Arabs al-tur means mountain. It was said: it is "the blessed." The majority held that it is the name of a mountain, as you say "Mount Uhud." It was said: Sayna' is a particular stone, and the mountain was attributed to it because it exists near it. It was said: it is every mountain that bears fruit.

The Kufans read Sayna' with a fatha on the sin, and the rest read it with a kasra on the sin. It is not declined (la yusrafa) because it became the name of a place. Al-Akhfash claimed that it is non-Arabic.

The majority read ﴿grows with the oil﴾ with a fatha on the first letter and a damma on the ba' (tanbutu). Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read it with a damma on the first letter and a kasra on the ba' (tunbitu).

The meaning according to the first reading is: it grows by itself, accompanied by the oil. According to the second reading the ba' is in the sense of ma'a (with), so it is for accompaniment. Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: the estimate is: its branches grow and the oil is with it. It was said: the ba' is superfluous. This was said by Abu 'Ubaydah, and similar to it is the words of the poet:
"They are free women, not mothers of asses, black-eyed, who do not recite the suwar."
Another said:
"We strike with the sword and hope for relief (bil-faraj)."

Al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: nabata and anbata have the same meaning. Al-Asma'i denies anbata and rejects this with the words of Zuhayr:
"You saw those in need around their homes, a settled community for them, until the herbage grew (anbata)."
That is, grew (nabata). Al-Zuhri, al-Hasan and al-A'raj read tunbatu with a damma on the first letter and a fatha on the ba'. Al-Zajjaj and Ibn Jinni said: that is, it grows and the oil is with it. Ibn Mas'ud read ﴿comes forth with the oil﴾. Zirr ibn Hubaysh read ﴿grows the oil﴾ by dropping the preposition.

Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Malik and al-Ashhab read ﴿with the dihan﴾ (dihan being a variant of the word for oil), and ﴿and a condiment (sibgh) for the eaters﴾ is coordinated with al-duhn (oil), that is: it grows with the thing that combines being an oil with which one anoints, and being a condiment with which one eats with bread.

The majority read sibgh, and a group read sibagh, like libs and libas. Every relish with which one eats bread is sibgh and sibagh. The original meaning of sibgh is what a garment is dyed with, and the relish was likened to it because bread with relish is like something dyed with it.

﴿And indeed in the cattle there is surely a lesson﴾. This is among the blessings with which Allah favoured them, and the explanation of al-an'am (the cattle) has already been given in Surat al-Nahl.

Al-Naysaburi said in his tafsir: Perhaps what is intended by al-an'am here is specifically camels, because they are what is ridden in the customary way, and because He paired them with the ship (al-fulk), which are the ships of the land, just as the ship is the ship of the sea. He, glorified is He, explained that they are a lesson, because they are among the things by whose creation and actions one is guided to the immensity of divine power. Then He, glorified is He, detailed what there is in these cattle of blessings after mentioning the lesson in them for the servants, saying: ﴿We give you to drink from what is in their bellies﴾. He means: the milk formed in their bellies and channelled to their udders. Indeed, in the transformation of what they eat of fodder into this delicious nourishment and this precious drink there is the greatest lesson for those who take heed and the greatest admonition for those who are admonished.

It was read nusqikum with the nun, on the basis that the agent is Allah, glorified is He. It was read with the upper ta' (tusqikum), on the basis that the agent is the cattle. Then He mentioned their benefits in general, saying: ﴿And for you in them are many benefits﴾, that is, in their backs, their milk, their offspring, their wool and their hair. Then He mentioned a particular benefit, saying: ﴿and from them you eat﴾, because of the great benefit of eating for them.

Likewise He mentioned riding upon them because of its great benefit, saying: ﴿And upon them and upon the ships you are carried﴾. That is: and upon the cattle. If by al-an'am is meant camels, cattle and sheep, then the meaning is: and upon some of the cattle, which are camels specifically. If by al-an'am is meant camels specifically, the meaning is clear.

Then, since the cattle are the most common thing one rides on in the land, He added to them what one rides on in the sea, saying: ﴿and upon the ships you are carried﴾, as a completion of the blessing and a perfecting of the favour.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: al-sulalah is the pure essence of the thin water from which the child is produced.

(p-980) … (p-981)

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "When the drop (nutfah) falls into the womb, it spreads into hair and nails, and it remains there for forty days. Then it slides down into the womb and becomes a clinging clot ('alaqah)."

The Successors (al-Tabi'un) had various opinions on the interpretation of *al-sulalah*, and we have already pointed out those views.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿Then We produced him as another creation﴾ that he said: "The hair and the teeth."

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from him concerning ﴿Then We produced him as another creation﴾ that he said: "He breathed the spirit into him." Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan, Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Rabi' (from Anas), al-Suddi, al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said the same, and Ibn Jarir chose this view.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Mujahid concerning ﴿Then We produced him as another creation﴾ that he said: "When youth came to him in full."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, 'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Salih Abi al-Khalil, who said: "When this verse was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ), up to His words ﴿Then We produced him as another creation﴾, 'Umar said: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾. He (ﷺ) said: 'By Him in whose hand my soul is, it has been concluded with what you have just said, O 'Umar.'"

al-Tayalisi, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn 'Asakir related from Anas, who said: 'Umar said: "I agreed with my Lord in four matters. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, if only we prayed behind the Station (of Ibrahim)!' Then Allah revealed ﴿And take from the Station of Ibrahim a place of prayer﴾. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, if only you would place a veil over your wives, for the good and the wicked enter upon you.' So Allah revealed ﴿And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a veil﴾. And I said to the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ): 'You must desist, or Allah will replace him with wives better than you.' So there was revealed ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you﴾, the verse. And there was revealed ﴿And We created man from an extract of clay﴾, up to His words ﴿Then We produced him as another creation﴾, so I said: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾."

Ibn Rahawayh, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat and Ibn Mardawayh related from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) dictated this verse, ﴿And We created man﴾, up to His words ﴿another creation﴾. Mu'adh ibn Jabal then said: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed, and Mu'adh said to him: 'What are you laughing at, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'With it, it was concluded: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾.'" In its chain is Jabir al-Ju'fi, who is extremely weak.

Ibn Kathir said: "In this report there is a severe strangeness, because this surah is Meccan, while Zayd ibn Thabit only wrote down revelation in Medina, and likewise Mu'adh ibn Jabal's conversion took place in Medina. And Allah knows best."

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Khatib (al-Suyuti said, with a weak chain) related from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah sent down five rivers from Paradise to the earth: Sayhun, which is the river of India; Jayhun, which is the river of Balkh; the Tigris and the Euphrates, which are the two rivers of Iraq; and the Nile, which is the river of Egypt. He sent them down from one spring among the springs of Paradise, from the lowest level of its levels, upon the two wings of Jibril. He entrusted them to the mountains and made them flow on the earth, and made them benefits for people in the kinds of their livelihoods. This is His saying: ﴿And We sent down water from the sky in measure, and We made it settle in the earth﴾. When Gog and Magog come out, Allah will send Jibril, and he will lift from the earth the Qur'an and knowledge, the Black Stone from the corner of the House, the Station of Ibrahim, the Ark of Musa with what is in it, and these five rivers. He will raise all of that to the sky. This is His saying: ﴿And indeed We are able to take it away﴾. When these things are lifted from the earth, its people have lost the good of this world and the Hereafter."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "Tur Sinin is the mountain from which Musa was called."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him concerning His saying ﴿growing with oil﴾ that he said: "It is the olive oil, which is eaten and used as an ointment."

It was also said that it is coordinated (ma'tufah) with what precedes it. By "man" is meant the genus (al-jins), because they were created within the creation of their father Adam. It was also said that what is meant is Adam.

Al-sulalah is on the pattern fu'alah, from al-sall, which is extracting one thing from another. It is said: "I drew (salaltu) a hair from the dough" and "the sword from its scabbard, so it slid out (fansalla)." So the semen-drop (al-nutfah) is a sulalah, and the child is a salil, and also a sulalah. From this is the words of the poet:
"She brought him forth, a sharp-edged, lion-like one, the offspring (sulalah) of a womb that was not secure."
And the words of another:
"Is Hind anything but an Arab mare, the offspring (sulalah) of mares whom a mule has mated with?"

The mim in ﴿from clay﴾ is explanatory (bayaniyyah), attached to an omitted element, and it occurs as a qualifier of sulalah, meaning: existing from clay. The meaning is that He, glorified is He, first created the essence of man from clay, because the origin is Adam, who was from pure clay, and his descendants are from clay and sperm.

It was said: the sulalah is clay, which, when you squeeze it, slips out from between your fingers, so what comes out is the sulalah. This was said by al-Kalbi.

Then ﴿We made him﴾, that is, the genus, by considering its individuals who are the children of Adam, or ﴿We made his offspring﴾, with an omitted noun, if by "man" Adam is meant: ﴿a drop (nutfah)﴾. If by al-an'am is meant camels, cattle and sheep, then the meaning is: and upon some of the cattle, which are camels specifically. If by al-an'am is meant camels specifically, the meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 23, verses 12–41 (part 1 of 2):

.
When He, glorified is He, urged His servants to worship and promised them Paradise (al-Firdaws) for doing it, He returned to establishing the origin (al-mabda') and the return (al-ma'ad), so that this would take firm root in the souls of the responsible (al-mukallafin). So He said: ﴿And We had certainly created man﴾ to the end of the verse. The lam is the answer to an omitted oath (qasam), and the sentence is independent (mubtada'ah). It was also said that it is coordinated (ma'tufah) with what precedes it. By "man" is meant the genus (al-jins), because they were created within the creation of their father Adam. It was also said that what is meant is Adam.

Al-sulalah is on the pattern fu'alah, from al-sall, which is extracting one thing from another. It is said: "I drew (salaltu) a hair from the dough" and "the sword from its scabbard, so it slid out (fansalla)." So the semen-drop (al-nutfah) is a sulalah, and the child is a salil, and also a sulalah. From this is the words of the poet:
"She brought him forth, a sharp-edged, lion-like one, the offspring (sulalah) of a womb that was not secure."
And the words of another:
"Is Hind anything but an Arab mare, the offspring (sulalah) of mares whom a mule has mated with?"

The mim in ﴿from a sulalah﴾ is for the beginning of the source (ibtida'iyyah), attached to khalaqna (We created). The mim in ﴿from clay﴾ is explanatory (bayaniyyah), attached to an omitted element, and it occurs as a qualifier of sulalah, meaning: existing from clay. The meaning is that He, glorified is He, first created the essence of man from clay, because the origin is Adam, who was from pure clay, and his descendants are from clay and sperm.

It was said: the sulalah is clay, which, when you squeeze it, slips out from between your fingers, so what comes out is the sulalah. This was said by al-Kalbi.

Then ﴿We made him﴾, that is, the genus, by considering its individuals who are the children of Adam, or ﴿We made his offspring﴾, with an omitted noun, if by "man" Adam is meant: ﴿a drop (nutfah)﴾. The explanation of the nutfah has already been given in Surat al-Hajj, and likewise the explanation of the clinging clot (alaqah) and the lump (mudghah).

By the firm abode (al-qarar al-makin) is meant the womb, and it is expressed by "abode" (qarar), which is a verbal noun, for emphasis.

The meaning of ﴿Then We made the drop a clinging clot﴾ is that He, glorified is He, transformed the white drop into a red clot. ﴿Then We made the clot a lump﴾, that is, a piece of flesh not yet shaped. ﴿Then We made the lump bones﴾, that is, Allah, glorified is He, made them hard so that they would be a backbone for the body, in specific shapes. ﴿Then We clothed the bones with flesh﴾, that is, Allah, glorified is He, caused flesh to grow over every bone in the amount that suits it and befits it. ﴿Then We brought him into being as another creation﴾, that is, We breathed into him the spirit after he had been an inanimate thing. It was said: We brought him out into the world. It was said: it is the growth of hair. It was said: it is the emergence of teeth. It was said: it is the completion of the powers created in him. There is no obstacle to intending all of these. The use of thumma (then) indicates the great difference between the two creations. ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾, that is, He deserves glorification and praise.

It was said: it is derived from barakah (blessing), that is, His good and blessing are abundant. Al-khalq in the language means measurement (taqdir). It is said: "I measured (khalaqtu) the hide" when you measure it in order to cut a piece from it. So the meaning of "the best of creators" is: the most skilful of makers who measure. From this is the words of the poet:
"Indeed you cut what you measure, and some people measure and then do not cut."

﴿Then indeed you, after that, will surely die.﴾ The reference in His words "after that" is to the preceding matters, that is: then indeed you, after those matters, are surely those who will go to death without doubt.

﴿Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, will be raised﴾ from your graves to the place of gathering (al-mahshar) for the reckoning and the punishment.

The lam in ﴿And We had certainly created above you seven paths﴾ is the answer to an omitted oath, and the sentence is independent, containing an explanation of the creation of what they need after the explanation of their own creation. The tara'iq (paths) are the heavens.

Al-Khalili, al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: they were called tara'iq because some of them were layered (tuwriqa) above others, like the layers of a shoe sole (mutarraqat al-na'l).

Abu 'Ubaydah said: "I layered (tarraqtu) the thing," meaning I made some of it above others, and the Arabs call everything above something else a tariqah.

It was said: because they are the paths of the angels. It was said: because they are the paths of the stars.

﴿And We were not unaware of the creation﴾. Here "creation" means the created things, that is: We were not unaware of these seven paths and their keeping from falling onto the earth.

Most of the exegetes said: what is meant is that We are not unaware of all creation; rather, We preserved the heavens from falling, and We preserved those on the earth from the sky falling on them and destroying them, or the earth shaking with them, or them perishing by some cause that would uproot them. It is permissible that what is intended is the negation of heedlessness regarding the maintenance of their interests and what they live by, and the negation of heedlessness regarding their protection.

﴿And We sent down from the sky water﴾. This is among the blessings with which Allah, glorified is He, favoured His creatures. What is meant by water is rainwater, for by it is the life of the earth and of the animals in it. Among that is the water of the rivers that descend from the sky, and of the springs and wells that are extracted from the earth, for their origin is from the water of the sky.

It was said: by this verse He, glorified is He, intended the four rivers: Sayhan, Jayhan, the Euphrates and the Nile. But there is no basis for this specification.

It was said: what is meant is sweet water. But there is no basis for that either, for there is no water on earth except that it is from the sky. The meaning of "in a measure" (bi-qadar) is by a measure from Us, or in an amount by which there is the welfare of crops and fruits, for if it were abundant it would bring about the destruction of that. Similar to it is His words, glorified is He: ﴿And there is nothing but that its treasuries are with Us, and We send it down only in a known measure﴾. The meaning of ﴿then We caused it to settle in the earth﴾ is We made it lodged in it, so that they benefit from it at the time of their need for it, like the water that remains in pools and puddles and the like. ﴿And indeed We are able to take it away﴾, that is, just as We were able to send it down, so We are able to take it away in some manner. The indefinite form here has a beautiful effect that is not hidden. In this is a severe threat, because of what it indicates of His power, glorified is He, to remove it and sink it deep, until people perish of thirst and their livestock perish. Similar to it is His words: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if your water should become sunken, who would bring you clear water?﴾

Then He, glorified is He, explained what results from the sending down of water, saying: ﴿So We produced for you therewith gardens of palm trees and grapevines﴾, that is, We brought into being with that water gardens of the two kinds mentioned, for you, ﴿in them there are abundant fruits﴾ with which you enjoy yourselves and of which you eat.

It was said: the meaning is: from these gardens are the sources of your sustenance and livelihood, like His words: "So-and-so eats from such-and-such a trade." This is far-fetched. He, glorified is He, limited the mention to palms and grapes because they are the ones found in al-Ta'if and al-Madinah and what is connected to them.

Thus said Ibn Jarir. It was also said: because they are the noblest of trees in fruit, and the best of them in benefit, taste and pleasure.

It was said that what is meant by His words ﴿for you in them are fruits﴾ is that for you in these gardens are fruits other than grapes and palms.

It was said: the meaning is that for you in these two kinds in particular are fruits, because in them are varieties differing in taste and colour.

The jurists have differed greatly over what the word "fruit" (fakihah) applies to. The best of what has been said is that it applies to the fruits that people eat, which are not a staple for them, nor food, nor condiment. Disagreement arose over whether vegetables (buqul) enter into fruit or not.

As for the accusative of shajarah (tree), it is in coordination with jannat (gardens). Al-Farra' permitted the nominative on the assumption: "and there is a tree," so it is raised as a subject (mubtada') whose predicate is omitted and estimated before it, which is the mentioned adverbial phrase.

Al-Wahidi said: all the exegetes say that what is meant by this tree is the olive tree. It was singled out for mention because no one tends it with irrigation, and it is the one from which oil is extracted. Allah, glorified is He, mentioned it as a favour upon His servants; and because it is the most noble of trees, the most widely beneficial, and the most abundant in blessing.

Then He, glorified is He, described this tree as ﴿coming forth from Mount Sinai﴾, which is a mountain in Bayt al-Maqdis. In the speech of the Arabs al-tur means mountain. It was said: it is "the blessed." The majority held that it is the name of a mountain, as you say "Mount Uhud." It was said: Sayna' is a particular stone, and the mountain was attributed to it because it exists near it. It was said: it is every mountain that bears fruit.

The Kufans read Sayna' with a fatha on the sin, and the rest read it with a kasra on the sin. It is not declined (la yusrafa) because it became the name of a place. Al-Akhfash claimed that it is non-Arabic.

The majority read ﴿grows with the oil﴾ with a fatha on the first letter and a damma on the ba' (tanbutu). Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read it with a damma on the first letter and a kasra on the ba' (tunbitu).

The meaning according to the first reading is: it grows by itself, accompanied by the oil. According to the second reading the ba' is in the sense of ma'a (with), so it is for accompaniment. Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: the estimate is: its branches grow and the oil is with it. It was said: the ba' is superfluous. This was said by Abu 'Ubaydah, and similar to it is the words of the poet:
"They are free women, not mothers of asses, black-eyed, who do not recite the suwar."
Another said:
"We strike with the sword and hope for relief (bil-faraj)."

Al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: nabata and anbata have the same meaning. Al-Asma'i denies anbata and rejects this with the words of Zuhayr:

Then He, glorified is He, detailed what there is in these cattle of blessings after mentioning the lesson in them for the servants, saying: ﴿We give you to drink from what is in their bellies﴾. Indeed, in the transformation of what they eat of fodder into this delicious nourishment and this precious drink there is the greatest lesson for those who take heed and the greatest admonition for those who are admonished.

It was read nusqikum with the nun, on the basis that the agent is Allah, glorified is He. It was read with the upper ta' (tusqikum), on the basis that the agent is the cattle. Then He mentioned their benefits in general, saying: ﴿And for you in them are many benefits﴾, that is, in their backs, their milk, their offspring, their wool and their hair. Then He mentioned a particular benefit, saying: ﴿and from them you eat﴾, because of the great benefit of eating for them.

Likewise He mentioned riding upon them because of its great benefit, saying: ﴿And upon them and upon the ships you are carried﴾. That is: and upon the cattle. If by al-an'am is meant camels, cattle and sheep, then the meaning is: and upon some of the cattle, which are camels specifically. If by al-an'am is meant camels specifically, the meaning is clear.

So the semen-drop (al-nutfah) is a sulalah, and the child is a salil, and also a sulalah. From this is the words of the poet:
"She brought him forth, a sharp-edged, lion-like one, the offspring (sulalah) of a womb that was not secure."
And the words of another:
"Is Hind anything but an Arab mare, the offspring (sulalah) of mares whom a mule has mated with?"

The mim in ﴿from a sulalah﴾ is for the beginning of the source (ibtida'iyyah), attached to khalaqna (We created). The mim in ﴿from clay﴾ is explanatory (bayaniyyah), attached to an omitted element, and it occurs as a qualifier of sulalah, meaning: existing from clay. The meaning is that He, glorified is He, first created the essence of man from clay, because the origin is Adam, who was from pure clay, and his descendants are from clay and sperm.

It was said: the sulalah is clay, which, when you squeeze it, slips out from between your fingers, so what comes out is the sulalah. This was said by al-Kalbi.

Then ﴿We made him﴾, that is, the genus, by considering its individuals who are the children of Adam, or ﴿We made his offspring﴾, with an omitted noun, if by "man" Adam is meant: ﴿a drop (nutfah)﴾. The explanation of the nutfah has already been given in Surat al-Hajj, and likewise the explanation of the clinging clot (alaqah) and the lump (mudghah).

By the firm abode (al-qarar al-makin) is meant the womb, and it is expressed by "abode" (qarar), which is a verbal noun, for emphasis.

The meaning of ﴿Then We made the drop a clinging clot﴾ is that He, glorified is He, transformed the white drop into a red clot. ﴿Then We made the clot a lump﴾, that is, a piece of flesh not yet shaped. ﴿Then We made the lump bones﴾, that is, Allah, glorified is He, made them hard so that they would be a backbone for the body, in specific shapes. ﴿Then We clothed the bones with flesh﴾, that is, Allah, glorified is He, caused flesh to grow over every bone in the amount that suits it and befits it. ﴿Then We brought him into being as another creation﴾, that is, We breathed into him the spirit after he had been an inanimate thing. It was said: We brought him out into the world. It was said: it is the growth of hair. It was said: it is the emergence of teeth. It was said: it is the completion of the powers created in him. There is no obstacle to intending all of these. The use of thumma (then) indicates the great difference between the two creations. ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾, that is, He deserves glorification and praise.

It was said: it is derived from barakah (blessing), that is, His good and blessing are abundant. Al-khalq in the language means measurement (taqdir). It is said: "I measured (khalaqtu) the hide" when you measure it in order to cut a piece from it. So the meaning of "the best of creators" is: the most skilful of makers who measure. From this is the words of the poet:
"Indeed you cut what you measure, and some people measure and then do not cut."

﴿Then indeed you, after that, will surely die.﴾ The reference in His words "after that" is to the preceding matters, that is: then indeed you, after those matters, are surely those who will go to death without doubt.

﴿Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, will be raised﴾ from your graves to the place of gathering (al-mahshar) for the reckoning and the punishment.

The lam in ﴿And We had certainly created above you seven paths﴾ is the answer to an omitted oath, and the sentence is independent, containing an explanation of the creation of what they need after the explanation of their own creation. The tara'iq (paths) are the heavens.

Al-Khalili, al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: they were called tara'iq because some of them were layered (tuwriqa) above others, like the layers of a shoe sole (mutarraqat al-na'l).

Abu 'Ubaydah said: "I layered (tarraqtu) the thing," meaning I made some of it above others, and the Arabs call everything above something else a tariqah.

It was said: because they are the paths of the angels. It was said: because they are the paths of the stars.

﴿And We were not unaware of the creation﴾. Here "creation" means the created things, that is: We were not unaware of these seven paths and their keeping from falling onto the earth.

Most of the exegetes said: what is meant is that We are not unaware of all creation; rather, We preserved the heavens from falling, and We preserved those on the earth from the sky falling on them and destroying them, or the earth shaking with them, or them perishing by some cause that would uproot them. It is permissible that what is intended is the negation of heedlessness regarding the maintenance of their interests and what they live by, and the negation of heedlessness regarding their protection.

﴿And We sent down from the sky water﴾. This is among the blessings with which Allah, glorified is He, favoured His creatures. What is meant by water is rainwater, for by it is the life of the earth and of the animals in it. Among that is the water of the rivers that descend from the sky, and of the springs and wells that are extracted from the earth, for their origin is from the water of the sky.

It was said: by this verse He, glorified is He, intended the four rivers: Sayhan, Jayhan, the Euphrates and the Nile. But there is no basis for this specification.

It was said: what is meant is sweet water. But there is no basis for that either, for there is no water on earth except that it is from the sky. The meaning of "in a measure" (bi-qadar) is by a measure from Us, or in an amount by which there is the welfare of crops and fruits, for if it were abundant it would bring about the destruction of that. Similar to it is His words, glorified is He: ﴿And there is nothing but that its treasuries are with Us, and We send it down only in a known measure﴾. The meaning of ﴿then We caused it to settle in the earth﴾ is We made it lodged in it, so that they benefit from it at the time of their need for it, like the water that remains in pools and puddles and the like. ﴿And indeed We are able to take it away﴾, that is, just as We were able to send it down, so We are able to take it away in some manner. The indefinite form here has a beautiful effect that is not hidden. In this is a severe threat, because of what it indicates of His power, glorified is He, to remove it and sink it deep, until people perish of thirst and their livestock perish. Similar to it is His words: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if your water should become sunken, who would bring you clear water?﴾

Then He, glorified is He, explained what results from the sending down of water, saying: ﴿So We produced for you therewith gardens of palm trees and grapevines﴾, that is, We brought into being with that water gardens of the two kinds mentioned, for you, ﴿in them there are abundant fruits﴾ with which you enjoy yourselves and of which you eat.

It was said: the meaning is: from these gardens are the sources of your sustenance and livelihood, like His words: "So-and-so eats from such-and-such a trade." This is far-fetched. He, glorified is He, limited the mention to palms and grapes because they are the ones found in al-Ta'if and al-Madinah and what is connected to them.

Thus said Ibn Jarir. It was also said: because they are the noblest of trees in fruit, and the best of them in benefit, taste and pleasure.

It was said that what is meant by His words ﴿for you in them are fruits﴾ is that for you in these gardens are fruits other than grapes and palms.

It was said: the meaning is that for you in these two kinds in particular are fruits, because in them are varieties differing in taste and colour.

The jurists have differed greatly over what the word "fruit" (fakihah) applies to. The best of what has been said is that it applies to the fruits that people eat, which are not a staple for them, nor food, nor condiment. Disagreement arose over whether vegetables (buqul) enter into fruit or not.

As for the accusative of shajarah (tree), it is in coordination with jannat (gardens). Al-Farra' permitted the nominative on the assumption: "and there is a tree," so it is raised as a subject (mubtada') whose predicate is omitted and estimated before it, which is the mentioned adverbial phrase.

Al-Wahidi said: all the exegetes say that what is meant by this tree is the olive tree. It was singled out for mention because no one tends it with irrigation, and it is the one from which oil is extracted. Allah, glorified is He, mentioned it as a favour upon His servants; and because it is the most noble of trees, the most widely beneficial, and the most abundant in blessing.

Then He, glorified is He, described this tree as ﴿coming forth from Mount Sinai﴾, which is a mountain in Bayt al-Maqdis. In the speech of the Arabs al-tur means mountain. It was said: it is "the blessed." The majority held that it is the name of a mountain, as you say "Mount Uhud." It was said: Sayna' is a particular stone, and the mountain was attributed to it because it exists near it. It was said: it is every mountain that bears fruit.

The Kufans read Sayna' with a fatha on the sin, and the rest read it with a kasra on the sin. It is not declined (la yusrafa) because it became the name of a place. Al-Akhfash claimed that it is non-Arabic.

The majority read ﴿grows with the oil﴾ with a fatha on the first letter and a damma on the ba' (tanbutu). Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read it with a damma on the first letter and a kasra on the ba' (tunbitu).

The meaning according to the first reading is: it grows by itself, accompanied by the oil. According to the second reading the ba' is in the sense of ma'a (with), so it is for accompaniment. Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: the estimate is: its branches grow and the oil is with it. It was said: the ba' is superfluous. This was said by Abu 'Ubaydah, and similar to it is the words of the poet:
"They are free women, not mothers of asses, black-eyed, who do not recite the suwar."
Another said:
"We strike with the sword and hope for relief (bil-faraj)."

Al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: nabata and anbata have the same meaning. Al-Asma'i denies anbata and rejects this with the words of Zuhayr:
"You saw those in need around their homes, a settled community for them, until the herbage grew (anbata)."
That is, grew (nabata). Al-Zuhri, al-Hasan and al-A'raj read tunbatu with a damma on the first letter and a fatha on the ba'. Al-Zajjaj and Ibn Jinni said: that is, it grows and the oil is with it. Ibn Mas'ud read ﴿comes forth with the oil﴾. Zirr ibn Hubaysh read ﴿grows the oil﴾ by dropping the preposition.

Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Malik and al-Ashhab read ﴿with the dihan﴾ (dihan being a variant of the word for oil), and ﴿and a condiment (sibgh) for the eaters﴾ is coordinated with al-duhn (oil), that is: it grows with the thing that combines being an oil with which one anoints, and being a condiment with which one eats with bread.

The majority read sibgh, and a group read sibagh, like libs and libas. Every relish with which one eats bread is sibgh and sibagh. The original meaning of sibgh is what a garment is dyed with, and the relish was likened to it because bread with relish is like something dyed with it.

﴿And indeed in the cattle there is surely a lesson﴾. This is among the blessings with which Allah favoured them, and the explanation of al-an'am (the cattle) has already been given in Surat al-Nahl.

Al-Naysaburi said in his tafsir: Perhaps what is intended by al-an'am here is specifically camels, because they are what is ridden in the customary way, and because He paired them with the ship (al-fulk), which are the ships of the land, just as the ship is the ship of the sea. He, glorified is He, explained that they are a lesson, because they are among the things by whose creation and actions one is guided to the immensity of divine power. Then He, glorified is He, detailed what there is in these cattle of blessings after mentioning the lesson in them for the servants, saying: ﴿We give you to drink from what is in their bellies﴾. He means: the milk formed in their bellies and channelled to their udders. Indeed, in the transformation of what they eat of fodder into this delicious nourishment and this precious drink there is the greatest lesson for those who take heed and the greatest admonition for those who are admonished.

It was read nusqikum with the nun, on the basis that the agent is Allah, glorified is He. It was read with the upper ta' (tusqikum), on the basis that the agent is the cattle. Then He mentioned their benefits in general, saying: ﴿And for you in them are many benefits﴾, that is, in their backs, their milk, their offspring, their wool and their hair. Then He mentioned a particular benefit, saying: ﴿and from them you eat﴾, because of the great benefit of eating for them.

Likewise He mentioned riding upon them because of its great benefit, saying: ﴿And upon them and upon the ships you are carried﴾. That is: and upon the cattle. If by al-an'am is meant camels, cattle and sheep, then the meaning is: and upon some of the cattle, which are camels specifically. If by al-an'am is meant camels specifically, the meaning is clear.

Then, since the cattle are the most common thing one rides on in the land, He added to them what one rides on in the sea, saying: ﴿and upon the ships you are carried﴾, as a completion of the blessing and a perfecting of the favour.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: al-sulalah is the pure essence of the thin water from which the child is produced.

(p-980) … (p-981)

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "When the drop (nutfah) falls into the womb, it spreads into hair and nails, and it remains there for forty days. Then it slides down into the womb and becomes a clinging clot ('alaqah)."

The Successors (al-Tabi'un) had various opinions on the interpretation of *al-sulalah*, and we have already pointed out those views.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿Then We produced him as another creation﴾ that he said: "The hair and the teeth."

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from him concerning ﴿Then We produced him as another creation﴾ that he said: "He breathed the spirit into him." Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan, Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Rabi' (from Anas), al-Suddi, al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said the same, and Ibn Jarir chose this view.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Mujahid concerning ﴿Then We produced him as another creation﴾ that he said: "When youth came to him in full."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, 'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Salih Abi al-Khalil, who said: "When this verse was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ), up to His words ﴿Then We produced him as another creation﴾, 'Umar said: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾. He (ﷺ) said: 'By Him in whose hand my soul is, it has been concluded with what you have just said, O 'Umar.'"

al-Tayalisi, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn 'Asakir related from Anas, who said: 'Umar said: "I agreed with my Lord in four matters. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, if only we prayed behind the Station (of Ibrahim)!' Then Allah revealed ﴿And take from the Station of Ibrahim a place of prayer﴾. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, if only you would place a veil over your wives, for the good and the wicked enter upon you.' So Allah revealed ﴿And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a veil﴾. And I said to the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ): 'You must desist, or Allah will replace him with wives better than you.' So there was revealed ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you﴾, the verse. And there was revealed ﴿And We created man from an extract of clay﴾, up to His words ﴿Then We produced him as another creation﴾, so I said: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾."

Ibn Rahawayh, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat and Ibn Mardawayh related from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) dictated this verse, ﴿And We created man﴾, up to His words ﴿another creation﴾. Mu'adh ibn Jabal then said: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed, and Mu'adh said to him: 'What are you laughing at, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'With it, it was concluded: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾.'" In its chain is Jabir al-Ju'fi, who is extremely weak.

Ibn Kathir said: "In this report there is a severe strangeness, because this surah is Meccan, while Zayd ibn Thabit only wrote down revelation in Medina, and likewise Mu'adh ibn Jabal's conversion took place in Medina. And Allah knows best."

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Khatib (al-Suyuti said, with a weak chain) related from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah sent down five rivers from Paradise to the earth: Sayhun, which is the river of India; Jayhun, which is the river of Balkh; the Tigris and the Euphrates, which are the two rivers of Iraq; and the Nile, which is the river of Egypt. He sent them down from one spring among the springs of Paradise, from the lowest level of its levels, upon the two wings of Jibril. He entrusted them to the mountains and made them flow on the earth, and made them benefits for people in the kinds of their livelihoods. This is His saying: ﴿And We sent down water from the sky in measure, and We made it settle in the earth﴾. When Gog and Magog come out, Allah will send Jibril, and he will lift from the earth the Qur'an and knowledge, the Black Stone from the corner of the House, the Station of Ibrahim, the Ark of Musa with what is in it, and these five rivers. He will raise all of that to the sky. This is His saying: ﴿And indeed We are able to take it away﴾. When these things are lifted from the earth, its people have lost the good of this world and the Hereafter."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "Tur Sinin is the mountain from which Musa was called."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him concerning His saying ﴿growing with oil﴾ that he said: "It is the olive oil, which is eaten and used as an ointment."

The meaning according to the first reading is: it grows by itself, accompanied by the oil. According to the second reading the ba' is in the sense of ma'a (with), so it is for accompaniment. Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: the estimate is: its branches grow and the oil is with it. It was said: the ba' is superfluous. This was said by Abu 'Ubaydah, and similar to it is the words of the poet:
"They are free women, not mothers of asses, black-eyed, who do not recite the suwar."
Another said:
"We strike with the sword and hope for relief (bil-faraj)."

Al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: nabata and anbata have the same meaning. Al-Asma'i denies anbata and rejects this with the words of Zuhayr:
"You saw those in need around their homes, a settled community for them, until the herbage grew (anbata)."
That is, grew (nabata). Al-Zuhri, al-Hasan and al-A'raj read tunbatu with a damma on the first letter and a fatha on the ba'. Al-Zajjaj and Ibn Jinni said: that is, it grows and the oil is with it. Ibn Mas'ud read ﴿comes forth with the oil﴾. Zirr ibn Hubaysh read ﴿grows the oil﴾ by dropping the preposition.

Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Malik and al-Ashhab read ﴿with the dihan﴾ (dihan being a variant of the word for oil), and ﴿and a condiment (sibgh) for the eaters﴾ is coordinated with al-duhn (oil), that is: it grows with the thing that combines being an oil with which one anoints, and being a condiment with which one eats with bread.

The majority read sibgh, and a group read sibagh, like libs and libas. Every relish with which one eats bread is sibgh and sibagh. The original meaning of sibgh is what a garment is dyed with, and the relish was likened to it because bread with relish is like something dyed with it.

﴿And indeed in the cattle there is surely a lesson﴾. This is among the blessings with which Allah favoured them, and the explanation of al-an'am (the cattle) has already been given in Surat al-Nahl.

Al-Naysaburi said in his tafsir: Perhaps what is intended by al-an'am here is specifically camels, because they are what is ridden in the customary way, and because He paired them with the ship (al-fulk), which are the ships of the land, just as the ship is the ship of the sea. He, glorified is He, explained that they are a lesson, because they are among the things by whose creation and actions one is guided to the immensity of divine power. Then He, glorified is He, detailed what there is in these cattle of blessings after mentioning the lesson in them for the servants, saying: ﴿We give you to drink from what is in their bellies﴾. He means: the milk formed in their bellies and channelled to their udders. Indeed, in the transformation of what they eat of fodder into this delicious nourishment and this precious drink there is the greatest lesson for those who take heed and the greatest admonition for those who are admonished.

It was read nusqikum with the nun, on the basis that the agent is Allah, glorified is He. It was read with the upper ta' (tusqikum), on the basis that the agent is the cattle. Then He mentioned their benefits in general, saying: ﴿And for you in them are many benefits﴾, that is, in their backs, their milk, their offspring, their wool and their hair. Then He mentioned a particular benefit, saying: ﴿and from them you eat﴾, because of the great benefit of eating for them.

Likewise He mentioned riding upon them because of its great benefit, saying: ﴿And upon them and upon the ships you are carried﴾. That is: and upon the cattle. If by al-an'am is meant camels, cattle and sheep, then the meaning is: and upon some of the cattle, which are camels specifically. If by al-an'am is meant camels specifically, the meaning is clear.

Then, since the cattle are the most common thing one rides on in the land, He added to them what one rides on in the sea, saying: ﴿and upon the ships you are carried﴾, as a completion of the blessing and a perfecting of the favour.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "When the drop (nutfah) falls into the womb, it spreads into hair and nails, and it remains there for forty days. Then it slides down into the womb and becomes a clinging clot ('alaqah)."

The Successors (al-Tabi'un) had various opinions on the interpretation of *al-sulalah*, and we have already pointed out those views.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿Then We produced him as another creation﴾ that he said: "The hair and the teeth."

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from him concerning ﴿Then We produced him as another creation﴾ that he said: "He breathed the spirit into him." 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Mujahid concerning ﴿Then We produced him as another creation﴾ that he said: "When youth came to him in full."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, 'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Salih Abi al-Khalil, who said: "When this verse was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ), up to His words ﴿Then We produced him as another creation﴾, 'Umar said: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾. He (ﷺ) said: 'By Him in whose hand my soul is, it has been concluded with what you have just said, O 'Umar.'"

al-Tayalisi, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn 'Asakir related from Anas, who said: 'Umar said: "I agreed with my Lord in four matters. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, if only we prayed behind the Station (of Ibrahim)!' Then Allah revealed ﴿And take from the Station of Ibrahim a place of prayer﴾. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, if only you would place a veil over your wives, for the good and the wicked enter upon you.' So Allah revealed ﴿And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a veil﴾. And I said to the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ): 'You must desist, or Allah will replace him with wives better than you.' So there was revealed ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you﴾, the verse. Mu'adh ibn Jabal then said: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed, and Mu'adh said to him: 'What are you laughing at, O Messenger of Allah?' Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "Tur Sinin is the mountain from which Musa was called."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 23, verses 12–41 (part 1 of 2):

.
When He, glorified is He, urged His servants to worship and promised them Paradise (al-Firdaws) for doing it, He returned to establishing the origin (al-mabda') and the return (al-ma'ad), so that this would take firm root in the souls of the responsible (al-mukallafin). So He said: ﴿And We had certainly created man﴾ to the end of the verse. The lam is the answer to an omitted oath (qasam), and the sentence is independent (mubtada'ah). It was also said that it is coordinated (ma'tufah) with what precedes it. By "man" is meant the genus (al-jins), because they were created within the creation of their father Adam. It was also said that what is meant is Adam.

Al-sulalah is on the pattern fu'alah, from al-sall, which is extracting one thing from another. It is said: "I drew (salaltu) a hair from the dough" and "the sword from its scabbard, so it slid out (fansalla)." So the semen-drop (al-nutfah) is a sulalah, and the child is a salil, and also a sulalah. From this is the words of the poet:
"She brought him forth, a sharp-edged, lion-like one, the offspring (sulalah) of a womb that was not secure."
And the words of another:
"Is Hind anything but an Arab mare, the offspring (sulalah) of mares whom a mule has mated with?"

The mim in ﴿from a sulalah﴾ is for the beginning of the source (ibtida'iyyah), attached to khalaqna (We created). The mim in ﴿from clay﴾ is explanatory (bayaniyyah), attached to an omitted element, and it occurs as a qualifier of sulalah, meaning: existing from clay. The meaning is that He, glorified is He, first created the essence of man from clay, because the origin is Adam, who was from pure clay, and his descendants are from clay and sperm.

It was said: the sulalah is clay, which, when you squeeze it, slips out from between your fingers, so what comes out is the sulalah. This was said by al-Kalbi.

Then ﴿We made him﴾, that is, the genus, by considering its individuals who are the children of Adam, or ﴿We made his offspring﴾, with an omitted noun, if by "man" Adam is meant: ﴿a drop (nutfah)﴾. The explanation of the nutfah has already been given in Surat al-Hajj, and likewise the explanation of the clinging clot (alaqah) and the lump (mudghah).

By the firm abode (al-qarar al-makin) is meant the womb, and it is expressed by "abode" (qarar), which is a verbal noun, for emphasis.

The meaning of ﴿Then We made the drop a clinging clot﴾ is that He, glorified is He, transformed the white drop into a red clot. ﴿Then We made the clot a lump﴾, that is, a piece of flesh not yet shaped. ﴿Then We made the lump bones﴾, that is, Allah, glorified is He, made them hard so that they would be a backbone for the body, in specific shapes. ﴿Then We clothed the bones with flesh﴾, that is, Allah, glorified is He, caused flesh to grow over every bone in the amount that suits it and befits it. ﴿Then We brought him into being as another creation﴾, that is, We breathed into him the spirit after he had been an inanimate thing. It was said: We brought him out into the world. It was said: it is the growth of hair. It was said: it is the emergence of teeth. It was said: it is the completion of the powers created in him. There is no obstacle to intending all of these. The use of thumma (then) indicates the great difference between the two creations. ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾, that is, He deserves glorification and praise.

It was said: it is derived from barakah (blessing), that is, His good and blessing are abundant. Al-khalq in the language means measurement (taqdir). It is said: "I measured (khalaqtu) the hide" when you measure it in order to cut a piece from it. So the meaning of "the best of creators" is: the most skilful of makers who measure. From this is the words of the poet:
"Indeed you cut what you measure, and some people measure and then do not cut."

﴿Then indeed you, after that, will surely die.﴾ The reference in His words "after that" is to the preceding matters, that is: then indeed you, after those matters, are surely those who will go to death without doubt.

﴿Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, will be raised﴾ from your graves to the place of gathering (al-mahshar) for the reckoning and the punishment.

The lam in ﴿And We had certainly created above you seven paths﴾ is the answer to an omitted oath, and the sentence is independent, containing an explanation of the creation of what they need after the explanation of their own creation. The tara'iq (paths) are the heavens.

Al-Khalili, al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: they were called tara'iq because some of them were layered (tuwriqa) above others, like the layers of a shoe sole (mutarraqat al-na'l).

Abu 'Ubaydah said: "I layered (tarraqtu) the thing," meaning I made some of it above others, and the Arabs call everything above something else a tariqah.

It was said: because they are the paths of the angels. It was said: because they are the paths of the stars.

﴿And We were not unaware of the creation﴾. Here "creation" means the created things, that is: We were not unaware of these seven paths and their keeping from falling onto the earth.

Most of the exegetes said: what is meant is that We are not unaware of all creation; rather, We preserved the heavens from falling, and We preserved those on the earth from the sky falling on them and destroying them, or the earth shaking with them, or them perishing by some cause that would uproot them. It is permissible that what is intended is the negation of heedlessness regarding the maintenance of their interests and what they live by, and the negation of heedlessness regarding their protection.

﴿And We sent down from the sky water﴾. This is among the blessings with which Allah, glorified is He, favoured His creatures. What is meant by water is rainwater, for by it is the life of the earth and of the animals in it. Among that is the water of the rivers that descend from the sky, and of the springs and wells that are extracted from the earth, for their origin is from the water of the sky.

It was said: by this verse He, glorified is He, intended the four rivers: Sayhan, Jayhan, the Euphrates and the Nile. But there is no basis for this specification.

It was said: what is meant is sweet water. But there is no basis for that either, for there is no water on earth except that it is from the sky. The meaning of "in a measure" (bi-qadar) is by a measure from Us, or in an amount by which there is the welfare of crops and fruits, for if it were abundant it would bring about the destruction of that. Similar to it is His words, glorified is He: ﴿And there is nothing but that its treasuries are with Us, and We send it down only in a known measure﴾. The meaning of ﴿then We caused it to settle in the earth﴾ is We made it lodged in it, so that they benefit from it at the time of their need for it, like the water that remains in pools and puddles and the like. ﴿And indeed We are able to take it away﴾, that is, just as We were able to send it down, so We are able to take it away in some manner. The indefinite form here has a beautiful effect that is not hidden. In this is a severe threat, because of what it indicates of His power, glorified is He, to remove it and sink it deep, until people perish of thirst and their livestock perish. Similar to it is His words: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if your water should become sunken, who would bring you clear water?﴾

Then He, glorified is He, explained what results from the sending down of water, saying: ﴿So We produced for you therewith gardens of palm trees and grapevines﴾, that is, We brought into being with that water gardens of the two kinds mentioned, for you, ﴿in them there are abundant fruits﴾ with which you enjoy yourselves and of which you eat.

It was said: the meaning is: from these gardens are the sources of your sustenance and livelihood, like His words: "So-and-so eats from such-and-such a trade." This is far-fetched. He, glorified is He, limited the mention to palms and grapes because they are the ones found in al-Ta'if and al-Madinah and what is connected to them.

Thus said Ibn Jarir. It was also said: because they are the noblest of trees in fruit, and the best of them in benefit, taste and pleasure.

It was said that what is meant by His words ﴿for you in them are fruits﴾ is that for you in these gardens are fruits other than grapes and palms.

It was said: the meaning is that for you in these two kinds in particular are fruits, because in them are varieties differing in taste and colour.

The jurists have differed greatly over what the word "fruit" (fakihah) applies to. The best of what has been said is that it applies to the fruits that people eat, which are not a staple for them, nor food, nor condiment. Disagreement arose over whether vegetables (buqul) enter into fruit or not.

As for the accusative of shajarah (tree), it is in coordination with jannat (gardens). Al-Farra' permitted the nominative on the assumption: "and there is a tree," so it is raised as a subject (mubtada') whose predicate is omitted and estimated before it, which is the mentioned adverbial phrase.

Al-Wahidi said: all the exegetes say that what is meant by this tree is the olive tree. It was singled out for mention because no one tends it with irrigation, and it is the one from which oil is extracted. Allah, glorified is He, mentioned it as a favour upon His servants; and because it is the most noble of trees, the most widely beneficial, and the most abundant in blessing.

Then He, glorified is He, described this tree as ﴿coming forth from Mount Sinai﴾, which is a mountain in Bayt al-Maqdis. In the speech of the Arabs al-tur means mountain. It was said: it is "the blessed." The majority held that it is the name of a mountain, as you say "Mount Uhud." It was said: Sayna' is a particular stone, and the mountain was attributed to it because it exists near it. It was said: it is every mountain that bears fruit.
